title: The strength that never slackens, not for a single second
subtitle: Al-Matin: the Firm, whose strength is steady, tireless and unbreakable
intro: Al-Matin (الْمَتِينُ) means The Firm, the Steadfast in strength: Allah's strength is so intense and steady that it never slackens, never tires and never wavers, holding up the heavens, the earth and every provision without pause. When everything you lean on bends or snaps, this name tells you the One you depend on never will.

root.sense: Matn is the back, the spine, and also hard, raised ground. From it comes matin: firm, solid, robust, like a rope that will not fray or a structure that will not buckle. Matin describes strength that holds under load. Applied to Allah, it is strength of perfect, unbroken firmness.

picture.label: Strength that holds under every load

knowing: Al-Matin appears once in the Quran, at the end of a short and striking passage: I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Me. I want no provision from them, nor do I want them to feed Me. Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm (51:56-58). {idea}He provides for every creature and needs nothing from any of them, and the strength behind that provision never weakens{/idea}.

Where Al-Qawiyy describes the completeness of His strength, Al-Matin describes its firmness: intense, steady, unwavering. Human strength comes in bursts and then fades; it needs rest, food and sleep. Allah is described as One whom neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes (2:255), who created the heavens and the earth and was touched by no weariness (50:38), and who holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease (35:41).

The same root describes His plan against those who persistently deny: I give them time; My plan is firm (7:183, 68:45). {trap}Delay is not weakness.{/trap} The rope He extends to the arrogant is long, and it does not break when He draws it in.
seeing: Every second, without your noticing, the earth turns at the right speed, the sun keeps burning, your lungs keep drawing breath and your heart keeps beating through the night. None of it pauses for maintenance. That relentless, silent steadiness is the signature of Al-Matin.

And every day, billions of creatures are fed: the ant in its tunnel, the bird that leaves its nest hungry, the newborn in a refugee tent. The verse that names Him Al-Matin calls Him first the Provider. The firmness of His strength is why provision never runs dry at the source.
trusting: We all lean on things that eventually give way. A job that felt secure, a body that used to be strong, a friend who always picked up. When they bend, the ground seems to move. {reward}Al-Matin is the one support that never shifts. Lean your full weight on Him, and it will hold.{/reward}

This name also speaks to people worried about provision. The One who said He wants no provision from you is the Provider with firm, unflagging strength. {idea}Your rizq is not held up by your boss's mood or the market; it is upheld by Al-Matin{/idea}. Work hard, and leave the anxiety at His door. The Quran calls faith grasping the firmest handhold, which never breaks (2:256).
loving: There is a particular love we feel for the person who never lets us down, who is there at 3am as much as at noon. Al-Matin is that in perfection: {reward}never tired of you, never worn down by your requests, never weaker today than yesterday.{/reward} The heart that knows Him stops bracing for abandonment.
now: It is the end of a brutal week: the car broke down, your mother is unwell, and work demanded everything. You are running on empty and feel guilty for having nothing left. {idea}Your strength was always meant to run out; His never does.{/idea} Before bed, say: Ya Matin, I am exhausted; carry what I cannot.
old: If I stop holding everything together, it will all collapse.
new: Al-Matin holds the heavens without tiring; I can rest and let His firm strength carry what I cannot.
try: When you feel worn out today, stop for one minute, breathe, and hand Him the specific load you are carrying by name.

dua.text: Ya Matin, Your strength never tires and Your hold never slips. When my strength fails, uphold me; when my supports give way, be my support; and keep me firm on Your path until I meet You.
dua.note: Call on Al-Matin when you are exhausted or anxious about provision, recalling 51:58, where He is the Provider, the Possessor of firm strength.

pairs.why: Joined in 51:58: Ar-Razzaq provides for all, and Al-Matin is the unflagging strength that keeps that provision flowing.
Al-Qawiyy is the completeness of His strength; Al-Matin is its steadiness, a strength that never wavers or rests.
Al-Qayyum sustains everything; Al-Matin is the firmness that means that sustaining never falters.

faq.a: Al-Matin means The Firm or The Steadfast in strength. It describes Allah's strength as intense, steady and unwavering, never weakening, never tiring and never needing rest, so that He upholds all creation and all provision without pause.

faq.q: Where is Al-Matin mentioned in the Quran?
faq.a: As a name of Allah it appears once, in 51:58: Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strength, the Firm. The same word describes His plan as firm in 7:183 and 68:45, meaning His respite to wrongdoers is not weakness.

faq.q: What is the difference between Al-Qawiyy and Al-Matin?
faq.a: Al-Qawiyy, the All-Strong, describes the fullness of Allah's strength. Al-Matin, the Firm, describes its intensity and steadiness: it never slackens or fluctuates. Scholars explain that one refers to perfect strength and the other to perfect firmness in that strength.

faq.q: Why is Al-Matin connected with provision?
faq.a: Because 51:56-58 says Allah wants no provision from people and is Himself the Provider, the Possessor of firm strength. The firmness of His strength is why the provision of every creature never runs out at its source.
